design_objective.primary: test whether prospective underwriting-gain discipline can reduce federal outlays while preserving producer service and insurer capacity

required_changes: create an express exception to SRA budget neutrality for legislatively specified underwriting-gain savings
permit those savings to reduce mandatory outlays instead of requiring recycling into A&O or underwriting-gain payments
retain existing A&O reimbursement protections, specialty-crop floors, high-loss-state payments, and inflation adjustments for the initial specification
require prospective application with no retroactive recovery of closed reinsurance-year gains
require public methodology, annual results, service-floor reporting, and five-reinsurance-year reauthorization or revision

policy_alternatives.description: retain the 2026 SRA and current statutory recycling and payment rules
prospectively calibrate reinsurance terms toward a 12-percent expected long-run AIP return on retained premium while leaving A&O policy unchanged
apply a current independently reproduced risk-adjusted market comparator using the same service and transition rules
pair underwriting discipline with audited cost-based A&O reimbursement

selected_score_specification.selection_reason: It isolates the historical excess-return question without cutting producer premium support or A&O delivery funding, and 12 percent has an official CBO option precedent. It is a scoreable test parameter, not a finding that 12 percent is currently optimal.

floor_rows.trigger: any covered unit loses all accepting providers
floor_rows.response: pause the affected term adjustment and authorize scored temporary stabilization

floor_rows.measure: approved provider count, entry, exit, capital, retained risk, and market share by state
floor_rows.trigger: provider count falls below two in an existing multi-provider market or falls more than 20 percent nationally from the frozen baseline
floor_rows.response: freeze the next adjustment and conduct competition and solvency review

floor_rows.measure: agent coverage, written agreements, policies, adjustment capacity, and claims by specialty status and high-loss state
floor_rows.trigger: materially worse access or timeliness beyond the general service trigger
floor_rows.response: retain statutory payment floors and apply targeted stabilization rather than across-the-board compensation

floor_rows.measure: submission error rate and processing turnaround
floor_rows.trigger: error rate exceeds 10 percent or median turnaround exceeds 7 days for two consecutive reporting periods
floor_rows.response: pause the next adjustment and require a corrective service plan

floor_rows.measure: claim timeliness, adjustment error, complaint, appeal, reversal, and producer-loss indicators
floor_rows.trigger: more than 5 percent deterioration from the frozen three-year baseline after risk adjustment or failure of an applicable legal standard
floor_rows.response: pause the next adjustment for the affected market and score remediation

required_inputs: projected retained premium and underwriting gains by reinsurance year
projected AIP participation, capital, risk retention, and behavioral response
mapping from reinsurance-year cash flows to federal fiscal years
federal administration, data publication, evaluation, and transition cost
interactions with producer premiums, indemnities, disaster assistance, and taxable income

next_evidence_action: Build a reproducible score-sensitivity and service-stress envelope for UW12_PROSPECTIVE using explicit retained-premium, gain, participation, implementation-cost, stabilization, and fiscal-year timing assumptions; keep all outputs illustrative until a matching current-law score and service-floor evidence exist.
